newsitem.title: USA: Clinton aide meets with UPS and Teamsters.
newsitem.headline: Clinton aide meets with UPS and Teamsters.

text.p: A senior White House aide met with officials from both the United Parcel Service and the Teamsters union, but a spokesman for President Clinton declined to speculate Thursday about intervention in the labour dispute.
"I'm not going to speculate on that at this point, we've just had contact with the parties to understand better their deliberations," White House spokesman Mike McCurry said.

Earlier Thursday, the Teamsters rejected what UPS had described as its final offer with a midnight strike deadline looming. However, both the company and the union say they will hold further talks if the other side is willing.
So far, the two sides have failed to agree on a wide range of issues that include pay and pensions, reducing the use of contract workers, more full-time positions plus health and safety matters.

McCurry said senior adviser Bruce Lindsey had met with the parties. It was Lindsey who play a prominent role earlier this year in White House intervention in the dispute between American Airlines and its pilots.
"Bruce Lindsey, I think at the request of both parties has met with them. It's mostly been an informational session," McCurry said. "I'm not aware that we've taken any formal role at this point."
